_README: BASELINE OF LINKS THAT RENDER UNDER THE 44px MOBILE TAP-TARGET FLOOR. This is a RATCHET, not an
allowlist. Recorded 2026-08-20 with the site-wide tap-target sweep in test/functional.spec.js.
Until then NOTHING in this repo measured tap-target size at all - tasks/backlog.md P6-50 said so
outright - and the gap shipped a live conversion bug (P6-61).
PAID DOWN FROM 12 CLASSES TO 2 ON 2026-08-21 (P6-62). What is left is P6-50's, and only P6-50's.
The ratchet forced this: every class fixed had to leave this file in the same PR, because the
sweep fails on an entry no page can still justify. Ten entries left at once for that reason.
EVERY NUMBER BELOW WAS MEASURED IN CHROMIUM AT 375x812, AFTER document.fonts.ready, not computed
from CSS. Both halves of that sentence were learned the hard way:
1. NOT COMPUTED FROM CSS. The first attempt at this gate parsed each page's CSS and computed
padding + border + line-box. It reported 61 broken pages where the browser found 5, because
`.hub-cta-row` is a flex container whose default `align-items: stretch` was quietly pulling
the short button up to its taller sibling's height. Do not replace this with a static check;
the full rationale is written out at the test.
2. AFTER FONTS LOAD. Inter loads late and fallback metrics are shorter, so a control near the
boundary reads short before the swap and fine after. 404.html's button measured 43px
pre-swap and 45px post-swap; it was never a defect and is not listed here.
THE SWEEP MEASURES THE HIT AREA, NOT THE BOX. Three card patterns on this site put the tap target
on the card rather than the label, via `::after { position: absolute; inset: 0 }` over a
positioned card: `.blog-link`, `.job-card-link` and `.read-more`. Their own boxes are 15-35px
while the real hit area is 327x498, 311x378 and 327x704. They were listed here until 2026-08-21,
which was wrong - they were never defects, and padding them would have been a fix applied to a
control that already passed. The sweep now walks to the positioned ancestor instead, and still
FAILS when that ancestor is missing or too small, which is exactly the bug P6-62 found on the 7
pages/blog/*.html category pages.
KEYED BY CLASS, NOT BY PAGE, ON PURPOSE. Keying by page would fail CI every time a new city hub
legitimately reuses `.brand-pill`, which turns the gate into friction to be silenced rather than
a signal to act on. An element is exempt if ANY of its classes appears below, so listing
`brand-pill` also covers `brand-pill premium`. THE TRADE-OFF, ACCEPTED AND STATED: a class listed
here spreading to more pages is NOT flagged. What IS flagged - the reason the gate exists - is
any short link whose classes are all absent from this list.
THE BASELINE MAY ONLY SHRINK. A class listed here that no longer measures under 44px on any page
FAILS the sweep with an instruction to remove it. Do NOT add a class here to make a failing run
pass: a newly short tap target is a bug in the page, not a number to record.
measuredWith: Chromium 375x812, after document.fonts.ready, via the test/functional.spec.js tap-target sweep
